gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced an overall gross strengthening of GBP 7.4 million on prior years' provisions in 2022. This deterioration was primarily driven by adverse development in energy, third party liability, and reinsurance accepted. These were partially offset by favorable development (releases) in marine, fire and other damage to property, and pecuniary loss. The 2019 year of account was notably impacted by COVID-19 related business interruption claims, particularly from Australia, leading to a loss on closure. The 2021 year of account was affected by significant natural catastrophe events such as Winter Storm Uri and Hurricane Ida, as well as the Russia-Ukraine conflict, which contributed to allocated loss reserves.
raw_causal_phrases: An overall deterioration of GBP 7.4 million on prior years' provisions was experienced during the year.

Deteriorations of GBP 3.1 million on energy, GBP 13.3 million on third party liability and GBP 6.0 million on reinsurance accepted were partially offset by improvements of GBP 3.0 million on marine, aviation and transport, GBP 4.7 million on fire and other damage to property and GBP 6.8 million on pecuniary loss.
This year remained open beyond its usual point of closing, affected by Covid-19 and the associated business interruption (BI) claims, particularly from Australia.
Disappointingly the challenges faced by this year of account mean that this year is closing with a loss of 10.1% of capacity.
Due to the timing of the awful events in the Ukraine, the majority of the syndicate's allocated loss reserves are sitting within the 2021 year of account.

The year was also affected by an unusual run of natural peril losses; winter storm Uri in February 2021 hit Texas with snow and a severe freeze and Hurricane Ida, the second most powerful storm to hit Louisiana after Hurricane Katrina of 2005
Syndicate 2121 has material exposure to losses arising from the Russia-Ukraine conflict and Covid-19 pandemic.
